Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1. List has been revised.
2. Original ossification test report has been received, which indicates the age of the victim to be between 15-16 years.

3. Heard Sri Vivek Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Arun Kumar Mishra, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
4. Learned A.G.A. has informed that the notice to the informant has been served on 23.10.2024.

sentences.text:
5. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.391 of 2024 (Session Trial No.96 of 2024), under Section 376(3) I.P.C., Section 3/4(2) POCSO Act and Section 3(2)(v) SC/ST Act, Police Station Baraut,
District Baghpat, during the pendency of trial.

6. The FIR was instituted against one Usman that too under suspicion, but subsequently the victim was recovered at Sonipat, Haryana and her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. was recorded and she has categorically stated that she was subjected to sex trade by her mother and she was taken by her neighbouring aunts to Haryana and thereupon she started living in the house of one Omviri and had married the applicant her-son.
Learned counsel has further stated that the victim has expressed her willingness to stay with the applicant only as she is his wedded wife.
7. Learned counsel for the applicant has also stated that it is true that the victim seems to be of slender frame, but she is major.
She is stated to be 15-16 years old as per ossification test report and a leverage of two years may be granted to the applicant on the upper side.
There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 27.06.2024 and he is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.
8. Learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application.

9. The Supreme Court in Jaya Mala vs. State of J & K, (1982) 2 SCC 538 and Mohd. Imran Khan vs.
State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi), (2011) 10 SCC 192 has opined that the radiologist cannot predict the correct date of birth rather there is a long margin of 1 to 2 years on either side.

sentences.text: A prima facie satisfaction of case is needed but it is not the same as an exhaustive exploration of the merits in the order itself.

11. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and taking into consideration the settled law of the Supreme Court passed in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690 and Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595 and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.

12. Let the applicant- Ashu, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
13. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

14. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.

15. The original ossification test report received shall be returned to the office of the C.M.O.
